summary: Türkiye Bursları (Türkiye Scholarships) is the Turkish government's fully funded award for bachelor's, master's and PhD study in Türkiye. It places you in a university and pays tuition, a monthly stipend, housing, health insurance, a return flight and a one-year Turkish language course. It suits applicants with strong grades, a clear study plan and a believable reason for choosing Türkiye.
lookfor: Academic success (grades above the minimum: 75% for master's/PhD, 70% for bachelor's, 90% for medicine, dentistry and pharmacy)
Motivation that fits the field and programmes you chose
Clear career goals and consistent programme choices
Social activities: volunteering, clubs, community work
How well you explain yourself and your plans at the 15–30 minute interview
cycle: The general programme opens 10 January and closes 20 February each year (expect about 10 Jan – 20 Feb 2027); evaluation March–April, interviews April–June, results early August, arrival in Türkiye September 2027. Check the official calendar for the confirmed 2027 dates.

eligibility.q: Are you a citizen of a country other than Türkiye (and have never held Turkish citizenship)?
eligibility.no: Turkish citizens and people who lost Turkish citizenship cannot apply. Look at domestic Turkish funding instead.

eligibility.q: Will you be under the age limit — under 21 for bachelor's, under 30 for master's, under 35 for PhD?
eligibility.no: If you are over the master's limit, consider a PhD application (under 35) if you qualify, or awards with no age cap such as Chevening or Commonwealth Scholarships. Check the current guidance for the exact cut-off date.

eligibility.q: Is your grade at least 75% (master's/PhD) or 70% (bachelor's), or 90% for medicine, dentistry or pharmacy?
eligibility.no: You will fail the preliminary check. Consider Stipendium Hungaricum or university-specific scholarships with lower thresholds.

eligibility.q: Will you have graduated (or be graduating by the end of this academic year) from the level below the one you are applying for?
eligibility.no: Final-year students can apply. If you will not finish by summer 2027, wait for the next round.

eligibility.q: Are you not already registered at a Turkish university at the same level you are applying for?
eligibility.no: Students already enrolled at that level in Türkiye are not eligible.

eligibility.q: Are you willing to spend one extra year learning Turkish (unless you already hold a C1 Turkish certificate)?
eligibility.no: All awardees without C1 Turkish must do the one-year language course. If you cannot add a year, this award is not a fit.

steps.title: Confirm you are eligible
steps.why: Applications that miss the age or grade limit are removed at the preliminary check, before anyone reads your essays.
do: Open the official application criteria and the 2026 brochure (links below).
Write down your date of birth and check it against the age limit for your level (under 21 / 30 / 35).
Find your grade on your transcript. If your university uses a CGPA (e.g. 3.8/5.0), note the exact figure and scale; the portal asks for it.
Check the minimum for your level: 75% for master's and PhD, 70% for bachelor's, 90% for medicine, dentistry and pharmacy.
If you are a final-year student, confirm you will graduate by summer 2027.
tips: If your grade is close to the limit, ask your faculty for an official percentage equivalent or a grading-scale letter to upload with your transcript.
avoid: Assuming a 'good second class' automatically equals 75% — check how your grade converts.
check: I can say yes to every must-have question above.

links.t: Türkiye Scholarships 2026 brochure (PDF, via Belize MFA)

steps.title: Understand how you will be judged
steps.why: Selectors look at grades, motivation, career goals, consistency of choices and social activities. Knowing this lets you plan every part of the form around it.
do: Open the 'Evaluation and Selection Process' page.
Write the five areas they assess on one page: academic success, motivation for the field, career goals, consistent programme choices, social activities.
Under each heading, list 2–3 pieces of evidence you already have (grades, projects, volunteering, jobs, NYSC service).
Note gaps (for example, no volunteering) and decide what you can show honestly.
tips: Undergraduate applicants also sit a short test (30 questions, 60 minutes, maths, geometry and logic). Practise basic maths if you are applying for a bachelor's degree.
avoid: Treating this as a pure grades contest; motivation and coherence matter at the expert and interview stages.
check: I have a one-page evidence list mapped to the five areas.

steps.title: Build your timeline backwards from 20 February
steps.why: The window is only about six weeks long. Most documents must be ready before it opens on 10 January.
do: Open the official application calendar.
Put 10 January (portal opens) and 20 February (closes) in your phone calendar, with reminders 30, 14 and 3 days before closing.
Set personal targets: documents scanned by 31 December, programme list by 5 January, statement draft by 10 January, submit by 10 February.
Add the interview window (April–June) and results (early August) so you keep your passport and certificates ready.
tips: Plan to submit at least a week early; the portal can be slow near the deadline.
check: All key dates are in my calendar with reminders.

steps.title: Choose up to 12 programmes
steps.why: You may list up to 12 university–programme choices in order. Coherent, well-ordered choices show focus and raise your chance of being placed.
do: When the portal opens, use its programme search to filter by level, field and language of instruction.
List 15–20 options in a spreadsheet: university, city, programme, language (Turkish or English), entry requirements (GRE/GMAT, language test).
Keep all choices in one field or closely related fields.
Mix well-known Istanbul/Ankara universities with strong universities in other cities.
Rank them in your real order of preference and cut to 12.
tips: Many programmes are taught in Turkish. That is fine — you will do the language year — but English-taught programmes may need IELTS/TOEFL.
Be ready to explain at interview why your top three are ordered that way.
avoid: Picking unrelated fields just to 'increase chances' — it looks unfocused.
Listing only the three most famous universities.
check: I have 12 ranked, related choices and know each one's requirements.

steps.title: Create your TBBS portal account
steps.why: Every application goes through the Türkiye Scholarships Information System (TBBS). It is free; no agent is needed.
do: Go to tbbs.turkiyeburslari.gov.tr and click to create an account (use an email you check daily).
Write down your username and password somewhere safe.
Fill in personal details exactly as on your passport.
Enter your education history and grades exactly as on your transcript.
Save and log out; come back to each section later.
tips: Applying is free. Anyone asking for money to 'guarantee' a place is a scam.
avoid: Grades in the form that do not match the uploaded transcript.
check: I can log in and my personal and education sections are complete.

steps.title: Get your passport and photo ready
steps.why: You need a valid ID or passport and a photo taken within the last year to submit.
do: Check your passport expiry date. If it expires before 2028, renew it now.
Nigeria: book a renewal on the Nigeria Immigration Service e-passport portal and attend your capture appointment; allow several weeks.
Take a recent passport-style photo on a plain white background.
Scan the passport data page in colour as a clear PDF.
tips: A national ID card is accepted for the application, but you will need a passport for the interview stage and visa — get it early.
avoid: An old photo or a selfie with a busy background.
check: I have a clear scan of a passport valid well into 2028 and a photo under one year old.

steps.title: Collect transcripts, certificates and test scores
steps.why: Your diploma (or provisional certificate) and transcript prove the grade threshold. Missing or unreadable files can sink an application.
do: Request your official transcript from your university's Academic Office / Exams and Records. Ask for a scanned copy you can upload.
Scan your degree certificate. If you have not received it, upload your statement of result or provisional certificate.
Final-year students: ask your faculty for a letter stating your expected graduation date and current grade.
Undergraduate applicants: scan your WAEC/NECO (or national exam) result.
If any programme on your list needs IELTS/TOEFL or GRE/GMAT, book the test now so results arrive before 20 February.
PhD applicants: prepare a research proposal and a writing sample (e.g. a thesis chapter or paper).
tips: If a document is not in English or Turkish, add a translation.
avoid: Booking an English test in late January — results may come too late.
check: Every required document is scanned, readable and named clearly.

steps.title: Write your statement of purpose / letter of intent
steps.why: This is one of the most important parts of the form. It is where you show motivation, career goals and why Türkiye.
do: Paragraph 1: the specific problem in your field or community that drives you (one real example).
Paragraph 2: what you have done so far — studies, projects, work, NYSC, volunteering — with results.
Paragraph 3: why this field and your top programmes; name what you want to learn.
Paragraph 4: why Türkiye (strengths in your field, regional links, culture) — be concrete.
Paragraph 5: your plan after graduation, in 2–3 sentences, and how you will connect Türkiye and your home country.
Paste into the portal, check the character count, and cut until it fits.
tips: Make it one argument: background → programme → future.
Name real problems and real outcomes instead of big words like 'passion'.
avoid: Copying a template from a blog.
Saying nothing about Türkiye or saying only 'it is beautiful'.
check: A stranger can tell, from my statement alone, what I will study, why, and what I will do after.
steps.prompt: Why this field, why these programmes, why Türkiye, and your plans after graduation.
steps.limit: Set in the TBBS form — check the current guidance

steps.title: PhD only: write your research proposal
steps.why: PhD applicants must upload a research proposal and writing sample; experts use them to judge readiness for research.
do: Choose a topic that fits the programmes on your list.
Structure: title, background and problem, aim and questions, methods, expected outcomes, timeline, key references.
Keep it short and precise (check any page limit in the portal).
Ask a lecturer to read it and comment.
tips: Show that the methods are doable in a Turkish lab or department.
avoid: A topic so broad it cannot be finished in a PhD.
check: My proposal has a clear question, methods and timeline.
steps.prompt: Research proposal for your intended PhD topic.

steps.title: Arrange recommendation letters
steps.why: The official how-to-apply page lists letters of recommendation. A teacher or employer who knows you well adds weight to your motivation and record.
do: Choose two people: a lecturer/supervisor and, if you work, your manager.
Send each a short request with your CV, programme list and statement draft.
Ask for a signed letter on letterhead by a date two weeks before you plan to submit.
Scan and upload the letters, or follow the portal's instructions if it asks for referee contact details.
tips: Pick people who know your work over 'big names' who barely know you.
check: I have two signed letters (or confirmed referees) ready.

steps.title: Complete, proofread and submit
steps.why: Only submitted applications are evaluated. Saving a draft is not enough.
do: Log in to TBBS and check every section: personal, education, activities, programme choices, statement, uploads.
Add social activities with dates and your role.
Confirm your 12 programme choices are in the right order.
Read the statement aloud once to catch errors.
Click submit and take a screenshot of the confirmation.
Check your email (and spam) for confirmation.
tips: Submit by about 10 February to avoid deadline-day portal problems.
avoid: Mismatched names or dates across documents.
check: The portal shows my application as submitted and I saved proof.

links.t: Watch: How to fill Turkey Burslari Scholarship Application form 2025 | Step by Step Complete Tutorial (Mudassar Chaudhry)

steps.title: Prepare for the interview
steps.why: Shortlisted applicants are interviewed (April–June) for 15–30 minutes, online or in person. Interview performance largely decides the final list.
do: Watch your email and TBBS for an interview invitation.
Reread your whole application, especially your statement and top three choices.
Prepare short answers: tell us about yourself; why this field; why Türkiye; why these universities; your plan after graduation.
Gather originals of all certificates — you must bring them.
Learn a few Turkish greetings; it shows genuine intent.
Do a mock interview with a friend or mentor.
tips: Prepare a three-sentence post-graduation plan you can say without notes.
avoid: Answers that contradict your written application.
check: I can answer the five core questions in under a minute each.

steps.title: Accept your award and prepare to travel
steps.why: Results come in early August and you move to Türkiye in September, so visa and paperwork must move fast.
do: Check TBBS in early August for your result and placement.
Accept the scholarship and follow the steps for the acceptance letter and scholarship agreement.
Apply for a student visa at the Turkish embassy or consulate using your acceptance documents.
Plan for the one-year Turkish language course (TÖMER) before your degree.
Book your flight only when the scholarship office confirms travel arrangements.
tips: The 2026 brochure listed monthly stipends of 6,500 TL (master's) and 9,000 TL (PhD); check current amounts and budget for your first weeks.
avoid: Resigning from your job before the visa is issued.
check: I have accepted, applied for my visa, and know my arrival date.

faq.a: No. Applying is free through the TBBS portal.
Some programmes are taught in English and may need IELTS/TOEFL. You still do the Turkish language year unless you hold C1 Turkish.

faq.q: How many programmes can I choose?
faq.a: Up to 12, ranked in order of preference.

faq.q: Do Nigerians need NYSC to apply?
faq.a: Türkiye Bursları does not ask for an NYSC certificate. Your degree and transcript are what matter.
Usually early August, with arrival in Türkiye in September.
